reviewConclusions: Private fresh output and copied native source closure isolate all six planned builds from the repository, registry binaries and existing services.
Original test source and fixture bytes are unchanged; only private bridge selection, transport capture and cleanup health checking are adapted.
Five single-point mutations cover exact division, serialized rule identity, systemId at same-key dereference, face/hole clipping, and capability preflight respectively.
Semantic kill requires native process health and the expected original AssertionError frame, with compilation failures, crashes, timeouts, skips and unrelated errors excluded.
ASan/UBSan flags, leak and halt options, and a 64 MiB child stack are explicit; this is a new 41+13 baseline, not a claim that historical 152 raw evidence was recovered.

Native stderr exists before process launch; stdout protocol lines and command/response journal are flushed while running, preserving completed transport evidence if the outer timeout kills the session.
Timeout and wait exceptions kill and reap only the command's own new process group. KeyboardInterrupt and SIGTERM stop further mutation work.

Each mutant restores the same private binary path to pristine bytes and reruns its original target method. The outer finally restores bytes without claiming a new oracle pass; a redundant final full baseline is not required.

resolvedFindings.originalProblem: An exception after successful Popen could leave the isolated child alive while outer cleanup restored the active binary.
resolvedFindings.resolution: command() now kills and reaps its own process group on exceptions and rethrows interruption; SIGTERM is handled as interruption.

resolvedFindings.originalProblem: Anonymous native stderr would disappear when the outer timeout killed the oracle before stop().
resolvedFindings.resolution: Native stderr is a named file created before launch, supplemented by flushed raw stdout and a live transport journal.

limitations: This receipt is source review and hash/AST inspection only. No compiler, native process, unittest suite, browser or driver help command was run by this reviewer.
Mutation survival or failure location remains unobserved until the root-owned serial run. A source prediction is not a mutation kill result.
Timeout may end the current incomplete protocol line; named raw stderr and previously flushed stdout/command records remain available.
